records.name: Proxima Centauri
records.type: High proper-motion M-dwarf / Alpha Centauri component
records.distance_basis: Direct inverse-parallax visualization distance; formal measurement uncertainty only.
records.description: The nearest known star to the Sun. Position, proper motion and parallax in this build are transcribed from the SIMBAD record, whose astrometry cites Gaia EDR3.

records.name: Sirius A / B
records.type: Spectroscopic binary; A-type primary + white dwarf
records.description: The brightest star system in Earth’s night sky. The position, proper motion, parallax and radial velocity shown here are catalog measurements surfaced through SIMBAD.

records.name: Vega (Alpha Lyrae)
records.description: A bright A-type standard star. SIMBAD lists the ICRS position, proper motion, parallax and radial velocity used in this embedded record.

records.name: Arcturus (Alpha Boötis)
records.description: A nearby orange giant with high proper motion. Astrometry and radial velocity are embedded from the SIMBAD record and its cited literature.

records.name: Pleiades Cluster (M45)
records.distance_basis: Inverse of the catalog mean parallax for atlas visualization; cluster depth is not represented.
records.description: The Pleiades open cluster. The embedded SIMBAD record reports a mean parallax of 7.364 mas and proper motion values from Gaia-era cluster astrometry.

records.name: Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis)
records.distance_basis: Naive inverse-parallax display distance; uncertainty/systematics are scientifically significant.
records.description: A nearby red supergiant whose distance is difficult to estimate precisely. v3 intentionally exposes the large uncertainty rather than presenting a false single-value precision.

records.name: Orion Nebula (M42)
records.distance_basis: Literature trigonometric-parallax distance to the Orion Nebula Cluster.
records.description: The Orion Nebula / Orion Nebula Cluster region. The sky position is from SIMBAD; the adopted distance is a published VLBA trigonometric-parallax result.

records.name: Sagittarius A* (Galactic Centre)
records.distance_basis: Geometric Galactic-centre distance from the S2 orbit.
records.description: The compact radio source associated with the Milky Way’s central black hole. Position is from SIMBAD; distance uses the GRAVITY Collaboration geometric S2-orbit measurement.

records.name: Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC)
records.distance_basis: Eclipsing-binary geometric distance; preferred over using local peculiar redshift.
records.description: A major Milky Way satellite and a cornerstone of the extragalactic distance ladder. Position and redshift are from SIMBAD; distance uses late-type eclipsing binaries.

records.name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
records.distance_basis: Adopted heliocentric Local Group distance 783 ± 25 kpc; redshift is not used as a Hubble-flow distance.
records.description: The dominant large galaxy of the Local Group alongside the Milky Way. The ICRS position and heliocentric redshift are from SIMBAD; a literature distance is adopted because peculiar velocity dominates locally.

records.name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
records.distance_basis: Adopted TRGB distance 809 ± 24 kpc; local peculiar velocity makes redshift unsuitable as a distance proxy.
records.description: The third-largest major galaxy of the Local Group. ICRS position and observed redshift come from SIMBAD; distance is a TRGB-based literature value.

records.name: Centaurus A (NGC 5128)
records.description: The nearest powerful radio galaxy. SIMBAD supplies the precise radio position and observed redshift; the adopted distance comes from a multi-method distance review.

records.name: 3C 273
records.distance_basis: Comoving distance numerically derived from observed z using this build’s Planck-2018-like cosmology.
records.description: The historically first identified quasar. Its precise ICRS direction and spectroscopic redshift are embedded from SIMBAD; radial distance is derived from that observed redshift under the atlas ΛCDM model.
